headline: IMF country numbers now on the record (The Times fresh write of Oct 13 WEO)
dek: Fresh write-up of the Oct 13 IMF October 2026 WEO with country detail not in our earlier record: Kuwait -16.7%, Iraq -16.0%, Qatar -15.6%, Bahrain -11.3% GDP in 2026; Saudi Arabia -3.3%, UAE -3.9%; Oman the exception at +4.1%. 2027 rebounds conditional on reopening: Iraq +19.0%, Qatar +18.8%,…
sources: The Times of London (<1h crawl) with IANS wire text of the IMF October 2026 WEO
fault_line: End the war to save the economy, or strike until Iran yields — who pays the 16%?

sections.what_happened: Fresh write-up of the Oct 13 IMF October 2026 WEO with country detail not in our earlier record: Kuwait -16.7%, Iraq -16.0%, Qatar -15.6%, Bahrain -11.3% GDP in 2026; Saudi Arabia -3.3%, UAE -3.9%; Oman the exception at +4.1%. 2027 rebounds conditional on reopening: Iraq +19.0%, Qatar +18.8%, Kuwait +17.1%, Bahrain +13.9%, Saudi +7.9%, UAE +7.7%. The Times adds: regional oil/gas output fell from 33m bpd (Feb) to a 19m bpd low in May; output likely fell further since August after Ansar Allah forces partially blockaded Bab el-Mandeb; Saudi fossil-fuel output at lowest of the year in recent weeks, but the kingdom resumed exports via the east-west pipeline to the Red Sea (7m bpd capacity). IMF: reopening Hormuz would produce a 'V-shaped' recovery, output bouncing back ~6.6% next year. MENAP region overall -0.3% in 2026 (already recorded at 1400-04).
sections.what_verified: IMF October 2026 WEO via IANS wire (ianslive.in, lokmattimes, punjabkesari, hiindia, menafn — consistent text and numbers). The Times business piece fresh <1h before scan. Note tension: WSJ/Kpler (Oct 22, recorded at 0100-01) said Hormuz+alternative routes shipped >24m bpd in the week through Oct 18, above the 23.3m bpd pre-war average — that is recent flows; the 33m→19m figures are output/production levels through May. Both can be true; do not conflate.
sections.what_disputed: All figures are IMF forecasts, not measured outcomes; the 2027 rebound assumes the conflict abates early 2027 ('exceptionally high uncertainty'). The Times cites the FT's Netanyahu-Oct-10 story (FT via 3 sources) as context — that is attributed reporting with a Netanyahu denial (see DNP/records 2026-10-21 1900-01).
sections.why_matters: The IMF prices the war in double digits: Kuwait's economy shrinks 16.7% while the war planners argue about strike dates. Pocketbook-first: what this costs every Gulf household vs what the strike planners say it buys. Present strictly as IMF forecasts.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261022-1400-04 — IMF country numbers now on the record (The Times fresh write of Oct 13 WEO): Kuwait -16.7%, Iraq -16.0%, Qatar -15.6%, Bahrain -11.3% GDP 2026; Saudi -3.3%, UAE -3.9%, Oman +4.1%; production 33m→19m bpd; east-west pipeline back (7m bpd)

totw_analysis: Our read: The IMF prices the war in double digits: Kuwait's economy shrinks 16.7% while the war planners argue about strike dates. Pocketbook-first: what this costs every Gulf household vs what the strike planners say it buys. Present strictly as IMF forecasts. The fault line our audience is arguing over: End the war to save the economy, or strike until Iran yields — who pays the 16%?
